To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the concentration of MT-I in the livers of C3H/2 mice is greater than that in the livers DBA/2 after Cd exposure, but this is not the case for MT-II; (2) the concentration of total MT (MT-I + MT-II) in C3H mice is greater than the concentration in DBA/2 at times after Cd exposure when the animals exhibit hepatotoxicity, but this difference is not present in animals exposed to Cd

the concentrations of MT-I, MT-II, and total MT were similar in the liver of C3H/HE and DBA/1 mice after exposure to non-toxic or mildly hepatotoxic dosages of cadmium, but the concentrations of these isoforms of MT were significantly higher in the liver of Cd-sensitive C3H/2 mice than in the liver of resistant DBA/2J mice after exposure to a mildly hepatotoxic dosage of cadmium.

the concentration of MT-I in liver of Cd sensitive mice is similar to that of Cd resistant mice at 6-12 hours after injection of Cd, but is greater than that of Cd resistant at 24-72 hours after Cd injection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of Cd-induced hepatotoxic injury.
elucidating the molecular basis for the genetic differences in the susceptibility to Cd hepatotoxicity.
the role of the endogenous protein metallothionein in the detoxication and metabolism of heavy metals, particularly cadmium and mercury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the susceptibility to Cd toxicity differs between C3H/ He and DBA/ 2 mice, and this susceptibility is not due to the inability to synthesize MT.

the Cd-induced hepatotoxic effect is due to a combination of factors including the inability of Cd-sensitive strains to increase the hepatic concentration of MT-II, a decrease in MT-I, and a decrease in the concentration of the non-metal-binding proteins in liver.
the susceptibility to Cd-induced hepatic injury in these two strains is due to an inherited difference in the capacity to detoxicate Cd.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cd toxicity is a complex phenomenon involving the induction of MT, the production of free radicals and the ability to handle the oxidative stress.
the Cd sensitivity of C3H/ He mice is due to the inability of these mice to detoxify the Cd that accumulates in the hepatocytes.
the susceptibility to Cd-induced hepatic toxicity is due to a genetic defect in the metabolism of the Cd-metallothionein complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Cd-sensitive and -resistant mice have similar concentrations of MT-I in liver after exposure to a hepatotoxic dose of the metal, and this suggests that susceptibility to Cd hepatotoxicity may not be mediated by a deficit in the accumulation of a particular isoforms of metallothionein.
the susceptibility to Cd-induced hepatic injury observed in C3He mice is not mediated by an inability to increase the concentration of hepatic MT in response to exposure to Cd.
the concentration of MT-I in the liver of Cd-sensitive C3H mice is greater than that in Cd-resistant DBA mice at 24-72 hours after injection with a mildly hepatotoxic dosage of Cd.
